Summary:
Quick but deep triage of yesterday's service degradation on Nomad Health staging that spilled into production during a billing spike. Focus on short-term rescue (operator-level fallbacks, throttle tuning) and mid-term mitigations (autoscaler thresholds, prefix/KV cache warmup, canary rollout patterns). Heavy participation from SRE and compliance to validate that mitigations don't violate data residency/KMS constraints.

Topics covered:
- Incident recap and suspected causal chain
- Immediate operator rescue options (fallback models, regional routing)
- Autoscaler thresholds and burst capacity tradeoffs
- Cache warmup / KV cache eviction strategies
- Security/compliance impacts of temporary test access and logs
- Next steps and ownership

Action items (read back during close):
- Priya to produce fallback tuning guide
- Jordan to run targeted load test and share results
- Evan to provide staging traces and firewall window
- Olivia to confirm compliance checkpoint items

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): alright hi everyone thanks for making time, um we'll keep this pretty focused, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, and Priya is our SE who'll do the deep config work today.
[00:12] Evan (SRE): hey Jordan, thanks. Quick note—apologies for the late ping yesterday, the spike started at about 03:14 UTC and our alerting only caught the tail.
[00:20] Priya (SE): yeah we saw the traces you uploaded, there's a clear tail latency increase and a bunch of in-flight requests stacking, looks like "prefix cache misses" + an autoscaler oscillation.
[00:33] Dr. Simone (VP Eng): to be clear, this is hitting production routing through our dedicated block, we saw customer-facing slowdowns for roughly 7 minutes.
[00:42] Jordan: ok, so top-level we should identify immediate operator-level fallbacks to bring latency down now and follow with a canary of tuned autoscaler parameters.
[00:52] Evan: can you explain "prefix cache misses" in plain terms? some of our newer folks weren't on that part yet.
[00:57] Priya: sure—Redwood keeps a prefix/KV cache to avoid recomputing long context, during that spike the cache got thrashed, likely from a rare query pattern that invalidated prefixes. When the KV cache misses we do more compute per request and that pushes GPU queues up. The other compounding thing was the autoscaler policy that scaled down too aggressively in low traffic, then when the spike hit it couldn't scale up fast enough.
[01:24] Rohan (Platform Eng): are we sure it's autoscaler slowness and not a scheduling delay on the infra side? the cloud shows some backlog.
[01:30] Priya: a mix—we saw queuing on the inference nodes and some VM start time variance. on the Redwood side the policies we use prioritize cost, so scaling is conservative unless you set burst capacity.
[01:44] Jordan: quick poll—do you want a conservative cost-safe fix (e.g., bump min replicas and add burst) or a latency-first fix (bump min + pre-warm cache)?
[01:53] Dr. Simone: latency-first, we can't have customer workloads impacted. We'll adjust cost later.
[01:58] Olivia (Compliance): note we need any run book changes captured, and if you want us to allow staging trace access we need a temporary access window documented. KMS keys can't be exported.
[02:09] Jordan: totally, we'll do a minimal access window, encrypted at rest and in transit—no key material leaves Nomad.
[02:14] Evan: here's a shorthand of what we saw: 1) unusual prompt pattern from a partner integration caused cache churn, 2) autoscaler scaled down trailing to the low traffic period, 3) sudden spike beat cold starts.
[02:27] Priya: recommended immediate operator steps—(A) enable small model fallback for 60 min on critical route, (B) set min replicas + burst pool to handle 3x usual p95, (C) increase KV cache size and set conservative eviction for 30 minutes. Those three together reduce queue and latency while we do a longer test.
[02:51] Rohan: fallback to smaller model sounds good, what's the quality delta? our downstream scoring expects high fidelity.
[02:57] Priya: for many user queries the smaller variant holds up, test showed about ~4% drop in answer quality for our eval set—tradeoff is temporary latency improvement from ~1.2s p95 down to ~320ms. we can gate fallback for non-critical endpoints.
[03:16] Dr. Simone: do the fallbacks require model weights to be stored in staging infra? anything that would violate residency?
[03:22] Priya: no, fallbacks are model variants already present in the dedicated pool; no additional data movement. we do need to ensure the model artifact is pinned in the same region.
[03:30] Evan: what's the risk if we bump min replicas—cost spikes?
[03:33] Jordan: yes, short-term cost bump; we can set an autoscale policy with a budget cap and time-window, plus burst pool that only kicks in during the next 60 minutes. we'll show the numbers in the load test results.
[03:45] Olivia: for compliance, anything we do for a 60-minute rescue must be logged and auditable—can you ensure audit logs are preserved?
[03:52] Priya: audit logs are preserved by default, but we will snapshot and hand them to you; we'll also add an annotation to the run explaining the temporary config.
[04:02] Jordan: ok live plan then—immediate operator play (within 15m): enable smaller-model fallback on the critical route, increase min replicas from 2->5 for 1 hour with burst pool size + pre-warm status, increase KV cache ephemeral size and conservative eviction. After that, run a 4-hour load test with your staging traces.
[04:21] Evan: timeline works, I'll open a firewall window 16:00-20:00 UTC tonight and push traces into the shared bucket.
[04:28] Priya: once we have traces we'll run two passes—one simulating the partner pattern that caused churn, one with even heavier synthetic burst. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:40] Dr. Simone: on the autoscaler tuning, what's the recommended policy? our current setting uses a 10m cool-down which seems long.
[04:46] Priya: we suggest shorter cooldown (60–90s) for targets where latency SLO is critical, plus a conservative scale-down step-size (don't drop more than 20% at once). Also set a warm pool for quick capacity. That avoids oscillation.
[04:59] Rohan: any change to cooldowns risk more churn in normal diurnal patterns though.
[05:04] Priya: correct, so we recommend a canary: change for critical route only and observe for 48 hours. If it looks good, apply to other routes.
[05:12] Jordan: also note—prefix cache warmup: we can pre-populate prefixes for your top 500 prompt families during the canary. That prevents cold misses and is cheap.
[05:22] Evan: how do you identify those top prompts? we don't want to leak user data.
[05:26] Priya: we only use hashed prompt signatures and frequency counts, no PII. We can work with your security team on the exact hash pipeline.
[05:35] Olivia: yes we need that pipeline documented; also KMS integration means logs remain encrypted with your key. we'll sign off if the hashes are done on-prem before sharing.
[05:45] Jordan: that's acceptable. We'll prepare an HLD doc for the hash-only pipeline.
[05:50] Priya: ops-level checklist for rescue (I'll paste to chat after call): 1) enable fallback, 2) bump min replicas + burst, 3) increase KV cache min size, 4) annotate run and snapshot logs, 5) run targeted load test.
[06:07] Evan: question about telemetry—do you have per-token timing breakdown so we can see whether the queuing is at model runtime vs GPU kernel enqueue?
[06:14] Priya: yes we have token-level traces; in your incident we saw the kernel enqueue time climb which indicates more compute not just network. that's consistent with cache misses.
[06:24] Rohan: is quantization an option to reduce runtime per token?
[06:28] Priya: yes, but it's risky for a short-term fix because it changes model behavior; it's in our mid-term mitigations (2–3 week timeline) not the immediate rescue. Could be part of a POC.
[06:38] Dr. Simone: can we have a schedule for the mid-term mitigation work? we'd like a timeline on prefix warming, canary autoscaler, and quantization POC.
[06:45] Jordan: propose: week 1 (this week) rescue + load test, week 2 canary with warmed prefixes and adjusted cooldowns, week 3–4 quantization POC and quality evals.
[06:56] Evan: that seems reasonable. I'll try to expedite the traces.
[07:00] Priya: on rollout mechanics—Redwood can do rollback on model pinning and we can set automatic fallback to hosted small model if a canary fails. Also we support per-route instrumentation so only one endpoint is affected.
[07:12] Rohan: are there any specific limiters we should set to block problematic partner patterns?
[07:17] Priya: rate limiting at the edge plus prompt-size caps we can enforce; also a short-circuit for known bad patterns. We can provide regex-like filters you can apply in your gateway.
[07:30] Olivia: security checkpoint—need a signed attestation for the staging access and confirmation that no PII is stored in Redwood logs beyond hashed IDs.
[07:39] Jordan: we'll provide attestation and a minimal SoW for the staging window.
[07:44] Evan: quick side question—why did the autoscaler reduce so aggressively? our metrics show the scale-down triggered while there was still sustained slow traffic.
[07:52] Priya: likely because our scale-down policy used a utilization metric averaged over 10m and didn't use queue depth as a signal. We'll propose adding queue depth and tail-latency metrics to the scaling rule.
[08:05] Dr. Simone: good—queue depth as a signal makes sense.
[08:09] Jordan: final thing—cost exposure. We'll include an estimated 1-hour cost delta for bumping min replicas + burst pool and compare that vs potential lost revenue from user-facing slowness.
[08:20] Evan: ok, so immediate windows—I'll share traces tonight at 16:00 UTC. Priya/Jordan will run tests and share the spreadsheet.
[08:28] Priya: yep and we'll also push the operator checklist to your runbook repo and annotate the change.
[08:35] Jordan: quick readback of next steps — (1) Jordan runs load test and shares sheet, (2) Priya drafts fallback tuning guide and checklist, (3) Evan provides staging access and traces, (4) Olivia confirms compliance gating, (5) schedule canary for week of Aug 17. Anything missing?
[08:52] Rohan: please add the queue-depth scaling rule proposal to the deliverables list.
[08:56] Jordan: added.
[09:00] Dr. Simone: thanks all—please send the security pack and attestation to Olivia; we'll reconvene after the canary.
